## Proof

**Yes**, such an orthonormal basis necessarily exists.

**Key observation.** For positive semidefinite matrices $A, B$, the condition $AB = 0$ forces the ranges to be orthogonal. Indeed, $AB = 0$ gives $\operatorname{range}(B) \subseteq \ker(A)$. Since $A$ is PSD (hence Hermitian), we have $\ker(A) = \operatorname{range}(A^*)^\perp = \operatorname{range}(A)^\perp$. Therefore
$$\operatorname{range}(B) \subseteq \operatorname{range}(A)^\perp,$$
i.e., $\operatorname{range}(A) \perp \operatorname{range}(B)$.

**Applying this to our setting.** Let $V_i := \operatorname{range}(P_i)$ and $r_i := \dim V_i = \operatorname{rank}(P_i)$. From $P_i P_j = 0$ for $i \neq j$, the subspaces $V_1, \dots, V_n$ are pairwise orthogonal in $\mathbb{C}^n$. Hence
$$\sum_{i=1}^{n} r_i = \dim(V_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus V_n) \leq \dim \mathbb{C}^n = n. \tag{1}$$

On the other hand, $\operatorname{Tr} P_i = 1 > 0$ implies $P_i \neq 0$, so each $P_i$ has at least one positive eigenvalue, giving
$$r_i \geq 1 \quad \text{for all } i, \qquad \text{hence} \quad \sum_{i=1}^{n} r_i \geq n. \tag{2}$$

Combining (1) and (2):
$$\sum_{i=1}^{n} r_i = n \quad \text{and} \quad r_i = 1 \text{ for every } i.$$

**Each $P_i$ is rank one.** A rank-one positive semidefinite matrix with trace $1$ has a single nonzero eigenvalue equal to $1$, so it takes the form $P_i = u_i u_i^*$ for some unit vector $u_i \in \mathbb{C}^n$.

**The $u_i$ form an orthonormal basis.** The range of $P_i = u_i u_i^*$ is $\operatorname{span}(u_i) = V_i$. Since the $V_i$ are pairwise orthogonal, we have $u_i \perp u_j$ for $i \neq j$. Thus $\{u_1, \dots, u_n\}$ is a set of $n$ mutually orthogonal unit vectors in $\mathbb{C}^n$, which is an orthonormal basis.

Therefore there exists an orthonormal basis $u_1, \dots, u_n$ of $\mathbb{C}^n$ with $P_i = u_i u_i^*$ for each $i$. $\blacksquare$
